— Additional Safety Tips","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Additional Safety Tips

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Defensive drivers stay alert with roaming eyes, spot brewing trouble early, hold a response plan, and honor the legal duty to shield others from their own errors [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
All riders in belt-equipped passenger vehicles, pickups, SUVs, and trucks must buckle up, and children under eight need approved car seats unless past four feet nine inches, since belts prevent ejection, dashboard strikes, and lost control [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Unbelted drivers face fines from twenty-five to fifty dollars, and the same band hits unbelted riders fifteen and up, while unsecured small children draw twenty-five to two hundred fifty, unbelted under-seventeens cost drivers one hundred to two hundred, and open-bed under-eighteens cost drivers twenty-five to two hundred [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Children under eighteen may not ride in open truck or trailer beds, though parades, emergencies, rural farm-worker shuttles, beaches, sole household vehicles, and permitted hayrides defend the charge [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A02
Towing a boat or watercraft with a rider under eighteen aboard is an offense, excused only by parade, emergency, or beach operation [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A02
Occupying a towed trailer or semitrailer is a Class B misdemeanor unless the tower was unaware, the space suits habitation, or the trip was a parade, emergency, farm shuttle, or permitted hayride [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A02
When signaled to stop, drivers pull fully right, park clear of traffic, engage parking gear and brake, shut off the engine, flash hazards, and light the dome lamp after dark [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A02
Stopped drivers stay seated with both hands on the wheel, crack the window when safe, take orders from either side, declare weapons, announce document locations before reaching, exit only when told, hold passengers inside, and signal out when released [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A02
Drivers must halt at once for emergency vehicles or risk arrest, though where stopping feels unsafe they may crawl with hazards lit, phone emergency dispatch while complying, or continue to a lighted public spot [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A02
Courtesy keeps everyone seated unless summoned, hands still until the officer nears, and handguns stored away from licenses and insurance [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A03
Stops are short investigative detentions where silence is protected yet licenses must be shown, arrestees must state name, address, and birth date, and false identities or answers invite arrest [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A03
Drivers may refuse vehicle searches, but probable cause or a suspected weapon lets officers search or pat down anyway, and resistance is unlawful even while voicing non-consent [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A03
Misconduct complaints go to the officer's superiors with agency and badge details, drivers never argue roadside, and a signed citation promises payment or a court date rather than admitting guilt [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A03
Falsely naming oneself during lawful detention is an offense, and fleeing an officer grows worse when wheels or watercraft aid escape or someone is hurt [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A03
Road rage wounds hundreds yearly, so drivers defuse it by planning routes, breathing through jams, tapping horns, signaling every lane move, refusing to block or tailgate, and reporting aggressors [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A04
Neighborhood electric vehicles meet Federal Motor Safety Standard 500 and cap at thirty-five miles per hour on flat pavement [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A04
Motor-assisted scooters carry at least two grounded wheels, reliable brakes, a forty-cc-or-smaller motor, a stand-or-sit deck, and human-power backup [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A04
Neighborhood electrics run only where limits read forty-five or less and scooters where they read thirty-five or less, and local governments may bar either for safety [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A04
Segway-style assistive devices balance one rider on two side-by-side wheels near seven hundred fifty watts, and may use sidewalks, bike paths, and slow residential streets only to cross, cover sidewalk gaps, or obey direction, hugging the right edge on roadways [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A04
Safe-driving keys span clear vision, law obedience, maintained cars, courtesy above right-of-way, faithful signals, and driving only when fit [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A05
Cargo beds must be solid, sided, front-closed, and rear-gated with loads tied front and back, while loose dirt-class freight needs boxed beds plus lashed tarps unless fully enclosed or riding below the rails [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A05
Cars and light trucks towing trailers must hitch DPS-approved safety chains, excepting farm trailers and federally compliant rigs [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A05
Tow links run 15 feet or less, hold the full weight, show a 12-inch-square white flag, and drag at most three front-lifted vehicles, save pole and pipe hauls [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A05
Carbon monoxide kills quietly, so drivers never idle in garages, trail traffic with open vents, idle sealed cars, drive on broken exhausts, or heat parked cars indoors, and they drag victims to fresh air and call 911 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A06
Texans with communication challenges may add an optional license code with physician-signed form DL-101 and flag vehicle registrations with form VTR-216 so dispatch alerts officers before they approach [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0075]
